candidate.claim: validate uses OR between undefined and null checks, so each condition is always true and errors are always reported even for complete payloads.
candidate.title: validation condition always true

verifier.reason: The conditions at src/validation.ts:8 and src/validation.ts:11 use || between !== undefined and !== null, which is tautologically true for any value, so both errors are always pushed even for complete payloads.

candidate.claim: buildSummary appends to module-level totals then aggregates over all of totals, so repeated calls double-count prior entries.
candidate.title: ledger summary accumulates across calls

verifier.reason: Confirmed: buildSummary at src/ledger.ts:12-15 calls post(entries) which pushes onto the module-level totals array at src/ledger.ts:6-9, then aggregates over all of totals without clearing it, so a second call re-includes prior entries.

candidate.claim: collect uses forEach with an async callback and returns results immediately, so promises are not awaited and the returned array is empty.
candidate.title: async forEach never awaited

verifier.reason: The code at src/analytics.ts:6 uses tasks.forEach with an async callback whose push at src/analytics.ts:7 occurs after an await, while src/analytics.ts:12 returns results immediately with no awaiting of those callbacks, so the array is empty at return.

candidate.claim: rotateToken calls store.save without await before store.get, so the read can race the write and return a stale token.
candidate.title: missing await on token save

verifier.reason: The interface at src/session.ts:2 declares save returns Promise<void>, and rotateToken at src/session.ts:11 calls store.save without await before returning store.get at src/session.ts:12, so the read can race the pending write.

candidate.claim: start overwrites this.timer with a new setInterval without clearing an existing interval, leaking the prior timer on repeated starts.
candidate.title: scheduler timer replaced without clear

verifier.reason: start at src/scheduler.ts:7-11 unconditionally assigns this.timer = setInterval(...) with no clearInterval or running check, so a second call orphans the prior interval.

candidate.claim: pageSlice slices with end+1, returning size+1 elements instead of exactly size elements.
candidate.title: page slice off-by-one

verifier.reason: At src/paging.ts:9-10 end is start+size and the return uses items.slice(start, end + 1), so a full page yields size+1 elements instead of size.

candidate.claim: sortScores uses default Array.sort without a numeric comparator, so numbers sort lexicographically and topScore can be wrong.
candidate.title: numeric sort without comparator

verifier.reason: sortScores at src/scores.ts:2 calls scores.slice().sort() with no comparator, so JavaScript sorts numbers lexicographically, and topScore at src/scores.ts:7 returns the last element which can therefore not be the numeric maximum.

candidate.claim: withinQuota uses strict less-than while its doc states max is inclusive, so a request using exactly max is incorrectly rejected.
candidate.title: quota inclusive bound uses strict less-than

verifier.reason: The doc at src/quota.ts:2-3 states max is inclusive, but src/quota.ts:6 returns used + amount < max, which is false when the sum equals max.

candidate.claim: normalizeSettings uses || for defaults, so legitimate 0 values for pageSize and budgetCents are replaced by fallbacks.
candidate.title: falsy default discards zero setting

verifier.reason: normalizeSettings at src/settings.ts:13-14 uses raw.pageSize || 20 and raw.budgetCents || 1000, so falsy 0 is replaced by the fallback, and src/settings.ts:18 states 0 is a legitimate value.
